Freedom 250 · Crypto · Reference · Crypto overview

The operators: which companies and networks run it, and how far along is each?

This page reads every operator the library tracks and how far along each one is, in one status vocabulary: 16 banks and asset managers across seven capabilities with where the proof stops, 32 card and processor products, 12 market systems, the money-machine seats; the bank transition, corporate stack and stack expansion comparisons; the Crypto Hub's 23 families with all 302 nodes and 372 connections; the field guide, the build-out ledger and the 112 vetted October 19 updates; and the 220 named actors and every placement. Announced is not live, and a partnership is not control.

    DTC Tokenization ServiceLive, limited

    Checked through: 2026-10-19 · Entity: DTC Tokenization Service, Depository Trust Company, DTCC, DTCC Digital (US) · Also shown on: Market plumbing
    Operator
    The Depository Trust Company (DTC), a DTCC subsidiary; software from DTCC Digital (US)
    What it does
    Lets DTC participants (the brokers and banks that hold securities at DTC) turn selected securities into tokens on approved blockchains and back again. DTC's own system (LedgerScan) stays the official record of who holds the tokens, and Cede & Co. stays the registered holder on the issuer's books. Eligible: Russell 1000 stocks, ETFs tracking major indexes, and U.S. Treasury bills, notes and bonds. At first the tokens carry no collateral or settlement value inside DTC.
    Status
    limited
    Status note
    Settled label: LIMITED. DTCC itself called the July 2026 run 'initial, limited production trades' (May 4 release) and the Jul 15 run used DTC's real production environment with real securities for several hours. It is not 'live': DTCC's own page still said 'expected October 2026 launch' when checked on 2026-10-19, and no DTCC announcement of the general launch was found. A KuCoin news flash (Oct 17) says the service launched for 25 securities, citing 'DTCC documentation'; this is unconfirmed.
    Regulatory status
    SEC staff no-action letter (Division of Trading and Markets), Dec 11, 2025: staff will not recommend enforcement if DTC launches a 'Preliminary Base Version'; the relief ends three years after launch. It is a staff position, not a Commission rule, and can be changed or withdrawn.
    Status history
    • Date: 2025-12-11 · Status: announced · What: SEC staff no-action letter allows DTC to launch the tokenization service's first version for three years; DTC expected launch in the second half of 2026.
    • Date: 2025-12-17 · Status: announced · What: DTCC and Digital Asset announce a plan to tokenize DTC-held U.S. Treasuries on Canton.
    • Date: 2026-05-04 · Status: announced · What: DTCC plans 'initial, limited production trades' in July 2026 and a service launch in October 2026; more than 50 firms in its industry working group.
    • Date: 2026-05-27 · Status: announced · What: DTCC and the Stellar Development Foundation expect DTC-tokenized assets on Stellar in the first half of 2027.
    • Date: 2026-07-15 · Status: limited · What: First production trades with DTC-tokenized assets over several hours: collateral pledges, securities lending, Treasury repo and stock trades where security and cash swap at once, and clearinghouse margin. DTCC's release says more than 30 firms; its later page says about 40. Networks: DTCC's private Besu network and the public Canton network.
    • Date: 2026-10-19 · Status: limited · What: DTCC's live-production page still says 'expected October 2026 launch'; no DTCC launch announcement was found.
    Chains
    • Name: LFDT Besu (DTCC's private network) · Status: limited · Since: 2026-07-15
    • Name: Canton Network (public) · Status: limited · Since: 2026-07-15
    • Name: Stellar (public) · Status: announced · Expected: first half of 2027
    • Name: Arc (Circle) · Status: announced · Expected: 2027
    Participants
    • About 40 firms took part on Jul 15, 2026 (DTCC page); more than 30 per DTCC's Jul 15 release.
    • Named in the library's Jul 15 record: BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan (tokenized QQQ holdings and posted tokenized collateral for CME margin), Vanguard, Circle, Nasdaq, NYSE.
    • Fireblocks says its wallets supported Citadel Securities in the July event.

    • Press (KuCoin, Oct 17) lists Circle's Arc as a planned network by 2027; no DTCC source found.

    Swift blockchain-based shared ledgerPilot

    Checked through: 2026-10-19 · Entity: Swift shared ledger, Swift
    Operator
    S.W.I.F.T. SC (Swift, a bank-owned Belgian cooperative company)
    What it does
    A shared ledger run by Swift on which participating banks record and move tokenized deposits that they themselves issue, around the clock including weekends. Swift coordinates the payment commitments; final settlement still happens afterwards through existing payment systems, and each bank stays responsible for its own deposits.
    Status
    pilot
    Status note
    Real money has moved in bank-reported controlled transactions, but banks call them 'live pilots' or a 'controlled proof of concept' and Swift calls this an 'initial controlled go-live phase'. No general availability date.
    Status history
    • Date: 2026-03-30 · Status: announced · What: Swift says design is complete and the minimum viable product is being built.
    • Date: 2026-07-09 · Status: announced · What: Swift says the ledger is ready for initial use; 17 banks are preparing to pilot live tokenized-deposit payments.
    • Date: 2026-08-19 · Status: pilot · What: Standard Chartered and HSBC report the first live tokenized-deposit transaction on the ledger.
    • Date: 2026-08-26 · Status: pilot · What: UOB and HSBC report completed Hong Kong-dollar transactions.
    • Date: 2026-09-02 · Status: pilot · What: Citi reports live U.S.-dollar transactions with FAB and OCBC; FAB says correspondent settlement completed.
    • Date: 2026-09-04 · Status: pilot · What: BNP Paribas and HSBC report a Siemens treasury payment, euros (France) to British pounds (UK).
    • Date: 2026-09-07 · Status: pilot · What: DBS reports a Saturday (Sep 5) U.S.-dollar payment from Singapore to Citi New York completed in minutes.
    • Date: 2026-09-28 · Status: pilot · What: Swift says 'most of the 17' banks have now used the ledger for 24/7 payments in five currencies (EUR, GBP, HKD, SGD, USD) between six continents; no banks named.

    Who has a full crypto money machine: the seats, firm by firm

    Read from: _Workspace/Indexes/masters/fed_access_and_charters.json › money_machine_* and crypto_companies_and_networks.json › banks.money_machine_seats

    How the seats are read

    Master checked through: 2026-10-19
    States
    • Label: Live · group-controlled · Meaning: Operating capability inside the named corporate group.
    • Label: Live · separately controlled · Meaning: Operating network, issuer or legal body outside the group's control.
    • Label: Live · bounded · Meaning: Operating capability with a narrower product, client or legal perimeter than the full seat.
    • Label: Approved / pre-opening · Meaning: A charter or approval clock exists, but the reviewed evidence does not establish an open operating service.
    • Label: Roadmap / rollout · Meaning: Announced, preview or future capability rather than general operating equivalence.
    • Label: No comparable layer · Meaning: No function equivalent to the Ripple baseline was established in this review.
    Seats (dimensions)
    • Label: Money / issuance · Question: Who issues the money or legal claim?
    • Label: Payments / distribution · Question: Who owns the customer route and payout orchestration?
    • Label: Custody / keys · Question: Who controls keys, safekeeping and return?
    • Label: Markets / prime · Question: Who supplies liquidity, credit, margin and execution?
    • Label: Corporate treasury · Question: Who runs the enterprise cash and treasury workflow?
    • Label: Network / ledger · Question: Who governs the ledger, sequencer or validator set?
    • Label: Bank / trust body · Question: Which licensed entity supplies custody, redemption, finality or remedy?
    Status map
    • Live owned: live
    • Live separate: live (operated by someone outside the group; not a status of the group itself)
    • Bounded: limited
    • Preopening: announced (charter.status conditional_approval or final_approval where a charter is the clock)
    • Roadmap: announced
    • Gap: not found
    About
    Legend of the Who Has a Full Crypto Money Machine page, copied as written. Its seat states (s) are the page's own words, not this file's status vocabulary; suggested_master_status_map is Claude's reading (2026-10-21) of how each state lines up with the spec_live_scale words and has not been reviewed.

    Fidelity

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Entity: Fidelity · Also shown on: Tokenized deposits
    Client access
    State: M5 Recurring production · Detail: Retail, wealth-management and institutional clients use Fidelity Crypto and Fidelity Digital Assets custody and trading routes; interested plan sponsors can add a bounded Digital Assets Account to a workplace plan. · Boundary: Eligibility, product availability and the responsible Fidelity legal entity differ by account, customer type and jurisdiction; a recordkeeping relationship does not authorize Fidelity to add an investment to every employer plan.
    Digital money
    State: M5 Recurring production · Detail: Fidelity Digital Assets National Association issues live FIDD, which eligible retail and institutional clients can purchase or redeem for one dollar and transfer to eligible Ethereum addresses. · Boundary: FIDD is the issuer's private stablecoin claim, not a bank deposit, FDIC- or SIPC-insured balance, central-bank money or legal tender.
    Assets & records
    State: M4 Bounded live · Detail: The live Fidelity Treasury Digital Fund OnChain class records a secondary representation of fund ownership on a public blockchain and reconciles it to the transfer agent's official book at least daily on business days. · Boundary: The transfer agent's book-entry record—not the blockchain—is the official ownership record; the disclosed fund size is not proven class-specific on-chain AUM.
    Custody & keys
    State: M5 Recurring production · Detail: Fidelity Digital Assets operates recurring institutional and retail custody and execution with hot/cold storage, transfers and an OCC-chartered national trust-bank seat; separate Fidelity workplace and trust entities provide plan recordkeeping, directed-trustee and custody functions. · Boundary: Crypto custody, DAA custody, plan-trust custody, recordkeeping and conventional brokerage custody are different seats; the national trust bank is uninsured and the exact plan agreement controls.
    Payment & settlement
    State: M5 Recurring production · Detail: FIDD purchase, redemption and Ethereum transfers are live, while Fidelity also offers real-time trade settlement and off-exchange settlement routes within its custody platform. · Boundary: Token transfer, customer-account credit, exchange settlement and final dollar discharge remain different events and may involve external liquidity providers or banks.
    Collateral & financing
    State: M4 Bounded live · Detail: The Collateral Account Suite supports cash loans from approved third-party lenders using bitcoin held at Fidelity Digital Assets as collateral. · Boundary: Fidelity acts as custodian and collateral agent; the lender, loan terms, valuation, perfection, default and liquidation rules remain route-specific and were not publicly named at transaction level.
    Scale & recovery
    State: M5 Recurring production · Detail: Fidelity operates recurring institutional, retail, wealth and stablecoin products with multi-site custody controls and redundant facilities. · Boundary: No public handled outage, redemption stress, record divergence, participant default, recovery or final-loss case completes M6.
    Kind
    Global asset manager, broker and national trust-bank digital custodian
    Domicile
    United States
    G sib
    No
    Thesis
    Build a vertically joined digital-asset ecosystem spanning direct client access, regulated custody and execution, a stablecoin, a tokenized fund share and collateral agency while retaining product-specific legal records.
    Frontier
    Connecting FIDD, the FYOXX OnChain class, custody and trading, and collateral accounts into interoperable retail and institutional routes with public exception and recovery evidence.
    Boundary
    Fidelity Investments, Fidelity Digital Assets National Association, Fidelity Management & Research, brokerage and workplace entities, plan fiduciaries, trustees, the fund and its transfer agent hold different legal and operating seats; group branding does not merge their claims or records.
    Watch
    FIDD circulation, reserve and redemption evidence; class-specific FYOXX OnChain scale and transfers; named collateral-loan/default routes; current DAA adoption and custody terms; any retirement-plan use of FIDD or tokenized funds; and a public correction, stress or recovery case.

    The liquidity-provider gap

    Home checked through: 2026-09-27
    Liquidity gap
    Liquidity provider remains an actor-and-receipt watch, not a technology category. The order distinguishes ordinary proprietary LP activity from the Covered Firm lane and requires committed or actually supplied own-account inventory, actual pool activity, compensation records and no-customer-custody evidence. Persistence, replenishment and hedging are separate operating tests, not automatic legal conditions.

    Ripple / XRPL

    Home checked through: 2026-09-01 · Entity: Ripple, XRP Ledger
    Kind
    company + public network
    Description
    Follow Ripple from the operating company through acquired product lines, exact regulated entities, RLUSD and XRP, XRPL transport, market access and the SEC proposal overlap.
    Boundary
    Ripple, its subsidiaries and products, XRPL, XRP and RLUSD are separate legal and technical objects; an edge records a reviewed relationship, not a merger of roles.
    Walkthrough
    • Steering: Ripple is the company parent; XRPL is a public network rather than a Ripple-owned subsidiary.
    • Operating stack: Payments, custody, prime brokerage, treasury and wallet services sit in distinct product and acquired-company branches.
    • Charter clock: Ripple National Trust Bank has preliminary conditional OCC approval but is not yet an operating national trust bank.
    • Asset control: Standard Custody is the named U.S. RLUSD issuer; XRP is XRPL's native asset, not Ripple equity or RLUSD backing.
    • Treasury and lending: Evernorth and Pathfinder are separate legal entities from Ripple; pre-close XRP remains under exact custody and escrow restrictions, while Evernorth's Single Asset Vault and XLS-66 participation remains proposed.
    • Execution: XRPL provides ledger, DEX and pathfinding functions; Wormhole and the XRPL EVM sidechain extend transport and application reach.
    • Cash and access: BNY holds the reviewed RLUSD reserve-custody and transaction-banking roles; Ripple Prime is separately an early adopter of BNY's private-platform tokenized deposits; exact Hidden Road entities hold reviewed DTC and FICC access.
    • Legal endpoint: Customer, issuer, custodian, transfer-agent and market-utility records remain decisive for title, redemption and settlement.
    • Policy overlap: Ripple's SEC submission is advocacy; proposal-fit edges show architectural touchpoints, not SEC adoption or approval.

    Controlled live pilots; no required public coin established. Bank claims, coordination, cash discharge and legal finality are separate.

    • Operator: SWIFT runs coordination; participating banks retain money and settlement responsibility.
    • Issuer: participating banks retain deposit liabilities; SWIFT does not issue this money.
    • Funding: SWIFT describes upfront confirmation; the precise reservation or credit object remains undisclosed.
    • Coordination: SWIFT operates the shared commitment ledger on Besu/EVM software.
    • Clearing: UOB and HSBC report matched and netted obligations before external settlement.
    • Cash: FAB reports completed correspondent settlement outside the SWIFT ledger.
    • Customer clock: DBS reports a September 5 weekend USD payment in minutes; external-finality timing is not specified.
    • Failure: executed participant terms, loss allocation and stressed performance remain unresolved.

    U.S. street-name equity (today)

    Home checked through: 2026-09-01
    Kind
    current stack
    Description
    How a broker-held cash equity clears and settles today: NSCC, CNS, DTC, Cede, NSS, settling banks. Overlay shows crypto attachments that do not replace those books.
    Boundary
    Solid nodes are the current machine. Overlay nodes are overlap, not overtake, unless that office’s T-account changes occupant.
    Walkthrough
    • Start with the street-name claim: the investor has an entitlement against a carrying broker, not title at the issuer.
    • Eligible broker-to-broker trades are captured in UTC and novated at NSCC. DTCC parent is not the CCP.
    • CNS nets one long or short per Member per security versus NSCC.
    • Securities move on DTC’s participant file. Cede stays the registered holder.
    • Money is not paid trade-by-trade. NSCC’s net, DTC as NSS agent, and the Fed’s NSS file debit settling banks.
    • 47 banks currently may act as DTC settling banks. Designation for a given member is not on this map.
    • Overlay: Hidden Road can sit as a DTC participant; DTC tokenization can re-represent the participant entitlement. Neither rewrites Cede or NSS.

    4 · Field guide, build-out ledger and the October 19 updates

    Field guide: what each technology is and what it does not control

    · 29 rows

    A differentiator is a useful architectural or operating distinction, not proof of adoption, market power, legal authority, production scale or token value capture.

    Read from: Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/Tokenization Entity and Control Map 2026-09-01/technology_field_guide.json

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03

    Ripple is not XRPL—and neither is XRP or RLUSD

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03
    Explanation
    Ripple is the operating company and product stack. XRPL is a public network. XRP is its native asset. RLUSD is a separately issued stablecoin claim. Their success, control and evidence ledgers must stay separate.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Securitize is not Ethereum

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03
    Explanation
    Securitize supplies regulated issuer, transfer-agent, brokerage/ATS, advisory and administration roles through named entities. Ethereum supplies public execution and consensus. A token can run on Ethereum while its legal ownership record and investor rights remain with Securitize, the issuer and governing documents.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Solana is the network; SOL is the native asset

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03
    Explanation
    Solana names the protocol, runtime and validator network. SOL pays fees and supports staking. Issued assets and applications on Solana retain their own operators, controls and legal records.
    Sources: none recorded on this row.

    Ripple / XRPLMeaningful

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Entity: Ripple, XRP Ledger
    Category
    Company & operating stack
    Ecosystem id
    ripple
    What it is
    A company-centered institutional digital-asset stack attached to, but legally separate from, the public XRP Ledger.
    Why following
    Ripple is assembling payments, custody, prime brokerage, treasury, wallet and stablecoin capabilities around institutional movement of value, while XRP Asia now adds a separable regional builder and systems-integrator distribution layer. That makes the stack relevant far beyond the retail idea of a payments coin.
    Differentiator status
    meaningful
    Differentiator
    The breadth of the operating stack: company products and acquired regulated entities can touch customer access, custody, liquidity, treasury and cash-like claims while XRPL supplies a separate public execution and pathfinding layer.
    Differentiator boundary
    Breadth does not make Ripple the owner of XRPL, the issuer of every XRPL asset, the legal recordkeeper for every tokenized security or proof that XRP is required in every Ripple route.
    How it works
    • A builder may enter upstream through XRP Asia, the XRP Ledger Foundation, XRPL Commons or another separate ecosystem-support body; those organizations do not inherit Ripple licences or product authority.
    • A customer or institution enters through a Ripple product or exact regulated affiliate.
    • The route may use custody, prime-brokerage, treasury or payment services depending on the job.
    • XRPL can provide ledger, exchange and pathfinding functions; XRP or RLUSD may play different asset roles.
    • Banks, issuers, custodians and legal recordkeepers still complete cash, title, redemption and remedy.
    Controls
    • Its products and controlled subsidiaries
    • Product design and commercial routing choices
    • Certain issued-asset or custody functions through named entities
    Does not control
    • XRPL as a public network
    • Every use of XRP
    • An issuer's legal register or bank settlement merely because the route touches Ripple technology
    Attachments
    banks, markets, records, cash
    Observed state
    Multiple current operating products and completed acquisitions coexist with conditional, proposed and advocacy-stage elements.
    Watch for
    • Exact product routes that require XRP rather than merely support it
    • XRP Asia program dates, funding, recipients, systems-integrator contracts and country-lawful mainnet deployments
    • Recurring institutional liquidity inventory
    • Operating evidence for conditionally approved or proposed entities and functions
    Do not confuse
    • Ripple company ≠ XRPL network
    • XRP ≠ Ripple equity
    • RLUSD ≠ XRP
    • XRP Asia ≠ SBI Ripple Asia ≠ Ripple Markets APAC
    • A Ripple policy submission ≠ SEC adoption
    Sources: Ripple Infrastructure Relationship Sweep (Read the full saved research: Ripple infrastructure relationship sweep; research notes) (2026-09-01) · Ripple cross-border payments product (2026-09-01) · Ripple closes Hidden Road acquisition (2025-10-24) · Ripple closes Standard Custody acquisition (2024-06-11) · Ripple written input to SEC Crypto Task Force (2026-05-22) · XRP Asia regional hub (2026-10-03) · SBI Ripple Asia company profile (2026-03-31) · MAS Financial Institutions Directory — Ripple Markets APAC

    SecuritizeMeaningful

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Entity: Securitize
    Category
    Company & operating stack
    Ecosystem id
    securitize
    What it is
    A public tokenization company whose named subsidiaries form a regulated securities-control plane across transfer agency, brokerage/ATS, investment advice, fund administration and an EU DLT trading-and-settlement venue.
    Why following
    It is one of the clearest places to see where a token becomes part of a real security: issuer authority, investor identity, the official register, transfer restrictions, corporate actions, trading access, redemption and correction.
    Differentiator status
    meaningful
    Differentiator
    It joins technology with a multi-entity regulated operating stack. Depending on the product, the transfer agent can maintain an off-chain control book across several token representations, a composite blockchain-plus-identity official register, or a token layer linked to an incumbent registrar.
    Differentiator boundary
    Regulatory registrations belong to exact subsidiaries and activities. They do not make Securitize a blockchain, a universal CSD or the sponsor of every fund it services.
    How it works
    • A fund or issuer creates the legal instrument and appoints the exact entities.
    • The transfer agent binds identity and eligibility to an account or whitelisted wallet and maintains the product-specific official record.
    • Securitize Markets can place or trade eligible securities; the adviser and administrator perform different appointed jobs.
    • A supported network carries token state or instructions while outside issuers, custodians and cash providers complete the legal and money legs.
    • The transfer agent can apply corporate actions and product-specific freeze, burn, reissue or correction procedures.
    Controls
    • Named platform and servicing functions
    • Its transfer-agent records, identity links, restrictions and correction workflows where appointed
    • Broker/ATS access for eligible products
    • Group-owned advisory and fund-administration operations
    Does not control
    • Ethereum, Solana, Tempo or another public network
    • A fund sponsor's investment mandate or issuer's corporate authority
    • Bank cash, reserve custody or asset custody outside the appointed arrangement
    • Every public company's primary register merely because Securitize supplies a token layer
    Attachments
    markets, records, cash
    Observed state
    Current U.S. regulated entities, live tokenized products, a 2026 public listing and CNMV-approved EU TSS coexist with partnership and production-volume clocks that remain product-specific.
    Watch for
    • Which record is legally authoritative for each product
    • Direct evidence for reported broker-dealer custody and atomic-settlement operations
    • BRSRV assets, stablecoin-reserve use and correction/outage evidence
    • Production instruments and volumes on the EU TSS and announced public-equity partnerships
    Do not confuse
    • Securitize Corp. ≠ each regulated subsidiary
    • Securitize Transfer Agent ≠ Securitize Markets
    • Token representation ≠ fund share by itself
    • AUM ≠ AUA ≠ transaction volume
    • Public-chain execution ≠ universal transfer-agent authority

    Category

    Differentiator status

    Ethereum finality does not decide who legally owns an off-chain claim, whether an issuer will redeem it or which intermediary must correct an error.

    • Protocol execution and consensus under adopted rules
    • Native fee and staking mechanics

    The TWIN/TLIP trade-document focus connects public-network proofs to multistakeholder trade workflows rather than treating the chain as the source of every document.
    Differentiator boundary
    The combination is promising but not an established unique moat; country implementations and payment functions remain on their own pilot or planned clocks.
    How it works
    • Public validators provide technical finality.
    • TWIN governance coordinates participating trade actors.
    • TLIP exchanges records and proofs across workflows.
    • Named agencies and issuers retain document authority; payment remains a separate layer.
    Controls
    • Public-network execution
    • Defined TWIN/TLIP workflow rules through their respective governance
    Does not control
    • Customs decisions
    • Identity issuers
    • The legal source record or future payment issuer
    Attachments
    records, cash
    Observed state
    Live technical components with pilot country implementations and a still-developing payment layer.
    Watch for
    Named production authorities, Legal recognition of exchanged documents, Actual payment and settlement design
    Do not confuse
    IOTA Foundation ≠ TWIN governance, IOTA token ≠ trade-document right, Proof exchange ≠ source authority

    WormholeContextual

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03 · Entity: Wormhole
    Category
    Connector & middleware
    Ecosystem id
    wormhole
    What it is
    A cross-chain messaging and interoperability layer connecting supported networks and asset representations.
    Why following
    Multi-chain finance needs transport between otherwise separate ledgers, and Wormhole appears across several tracked issuer and network relationships.
    Differentiator status
    contextual
    Differentiator
    Broad cross-chain connectivity and named integrations make it an important transport layer in this map.
    Differentiator boundary
    Connectivity is not a unique legal or monetary advantage. Wormhole does not supply the issuer promise, legal register, reserve, bank cash or ultimate remedy.
    How it works
    • A supported source-chain event creates a message or transfer instruction.
    • Wormhole's verification design carries that information across environments.
    • A destination-chain representation or action is created under integration rules.
    • Issuer, transfer agent, custodian and cash rail remain external authorities.
    Controls
    Its messaging and verification layer, Supported integration mechanics
    Does not control
    Source or destination chain governance, Asset issuance and redemption, Legal title and cash settlement
    Attachments
    markets, records, cash
    Observed state
    Live interoperability technology with integration-by-integration operating evidence.
    Watch for
    • Recovery when ledgers disagree
    • Authoritative supply and burn/mint controls
    • Whether a route is live, announced or only supported in principle
    Do not confuse
    Transport ≠ issuer authority, Cross-chain representation ≠ legal title, Message completion ≠ cash discharge

    SWIFT ledger & bank obligationsMeaningful

    Home checked through: 2026-10-03
    Category
    Market infrastructure
    Ecosystem id
    swift-ledger
    What it is
    A bank-coordination design in which Swift operates shared commitment infrastructure while participant banks retain the underlying money obligations.
    Why following
    It demonstrates that shared-ledger coordination can grow without a public coin and without stripping banks of their deposit liabilities or external settlement responsibilities.
    Differentiator status
    meaningful
    Differentiator
    A trusted cooperative messaging network is extending into shared commitment coordination on EVM-compatible technology while preserving bank-issued money and existing settlement systems.
    Differentiator boundary
    Pilot completion does not establish general availability, public-coin use, exact funding treatment, finality timing or stressed loss allocation.
    How it works
    • Participating banks establish customer and interbank obligations.
    • Swift coordinates confirmed commitments on the shared ledger.
    • Some obligations can be matched or netted in the workflow.
    • Banks and existing systems complete correspondent or settlement cash outside the shared ledger where required.
    Controls
    • Shared coordination infrastructure
    • Participant rules and messaging workflow through the cooperative framework
    Does not control
    • Participant deposit liabilities
    • Every bank's customer books
    • External cash settlement merely by recording a commitment
    Attachments
    banks, markets, records, cash
    Observed state
    Controlled live pilots with named participants and completed pairings; general production and stress evidence remain open.
    Watch for
    • Executed participant terms
    • Funding reservation and liquidity mechanics
    • External settlement timing
    • Production scale and failure allocation
    Do not confuse
    • Swift cooperative ≠ participant banks
    • Shared ledger commitment ≠ bank money
    • Matched obligation ≠ final cash settlement

    Headline
    Ripple's stack combines company-reported live institutional uses with a newly live XRP Asia regional builder layer; the organization expands XRPL distribution capacity without creating a payment route or XRP demand receipt.
    Strongest receipt
    CSD BR remains the strongest operating receipt: real BTG Pactual fund-share records, Ripple Custody and XRPL MPTs in a live-environment first phase while CSD BR retains the official registration, deposit and settlement record. XRP Asia is a separate organizational receipt upstream of products and transactions.
    Current builds
    • Name: XRP Asia regional builder and integrator hub · State: live available · Date: 2026-10-03 · Summary: XRP Asia Ltd launched a Singapore-based public hub and intake with visible Singapore, Tokyo and Seoul community nodes and support paths for developers, systems integrators, startups, partners and ambassadors. · Boundary: Programs and dates remain forthcoming. Ownership, budget, awards and deployments are undisclosed, and the hub is not a financial licence, token issuer, validator authority or payment rail.
    • Name: CSD BR XRPL fund-share record mirror · State: live named use · Date: 2026-09-29 · Summary: Selected BTG Pactual fund-share records deposited at CSD BR are to be mirrored as permissioned XRPL MPTs for query, audit and near-real-time consistency checks. · Boundary: CSD BR's conventional systems remain authoritative. Company-reported live use is not yet independently reproducible because no issuer account, MPT issuance ID, transaction hash, named fund/class, amount or reconciliation result was published.
    • Name: Ripple Mint · State: live available · Date: 2026-07-23 · Summary: UI and APIs for eligible customers to mint, redeem, bridge and monitor RLUSD. · Boundary: Availability is not usage scale and does not make XRP the settlement asset.
    • Name: XRPL Lending Protocol · State: testnet · Date: 2026-06-29 · Summary: Native fixed-term credit primitives under XLS-65 and XLS-66. · Boundary: Devnet work is subject to validator approval; credit underwriting stays offchain.
    Deals and integrations
    • Counterparty: XRP Asia, XRP Ledger Foundation and XRPL Commons · Date: 2026-10-03 · State: live available · Summary: A regional builder organization now sits beside separate global protocol and community-support bodies, with Ripple ecosystem personnel supporting the launch. · Boundary: Coordination does not establish common ownership, shared financial liability, validator control, bank adoption or use of RLUSD or XRP.
    • Counterparty: CSD BR and BTG Pactual · Date: 2026-09-29 · State: live named use · Summary: First-phase partnership joins Ripple Custody and XRPL MPTs to CSD BR's regulated fund-share record workflow. · Boundary: This is record mirroring, not XRPL legal-title authority or cash settlement; it does not disclose RLUSD use, XRP bridge liquidity or movement of CSD BR's aggregate R$22 trillion registered-asset base onto XRPL.
    • Counterparty: Hidden Road / Ripple Prime · Date: 2026 · State: live named use · Summary: Acquired prime-brokerage capability broadens Ripple's institutional stack. · Boundary: Corporate ownership does not prove XRPL or XRP is used in every prime transaction.
    Native token
    • Symbol: XRP
    • Role: XRPL fees, reserves and optional bridge liquidity
    • Required channel: Required for XRPL protocol fees and account/object reserves; not universally required by Ripple enterprise products or RLUSD flows.
    • Value capture: Network activity can consume small XRP fees and require reserves, but institutional deal announcements do not establish material XRP demand.
    Transition assessment
    • What changed: A regulated Brazilian market-infrastructure operator named XRPL as a public-chain record mirror, while XRP Asia separately moved from concept to a live regional builder and integrator hub.
    • Live now: Company-reported CSD BR record mirroring, Ripple payments, custody and prime services, eligible-customer RLUSD minting, and XRP Asia organizational intake.
    • Still building: XRP Asia programs, awards, integrator contracts and country-lawful deployments; public operating receipts for the CSD BR mirror; native lending; and any later native issuance or trading phase.
    • Not proved: That XRP Asia is a payment rail or Ripple subsidiary, that its communities create bank adoption, that XRPL is the Brazilian legal record or cash-settlement rail, or that Ripple and XRPL growth require material XRP inventory.
    Return gates
    • XRP Asia ownership, governance, funding, dated programs, named recipients and mainnet deployment receipts
    • Country-specific systems-integrator contracts and exact licensed legal persons
    • CSD BR issuer account, MPT issuance ID, exact fund/class, transaction hashes, mirrored value and reconciliation results
    • Validator approval and mainnet activation of XLS-65/66
    • Auditable disclosure connecting institutional volume to XRP use
    Sources: XRP Asia regional hub (2026-10-03) · XRP Asia privacy policy (2026-09-25) · Supporting Innovation on the XRP Ledger: What's Changing in 2026 (2026-02-26) · CSD BR and Ripple XRPL record-mirroring partnership (2026-09-29) · XRPL Multi-Purpose Token documentation · Ripple Mint launch (2026-07-23) · XRPL Lending Protocol (2026-06-29) · Ripple Swell 2026 ecosystem lineup (2026-09-29) · Ripple closes Hidden Road acquisition (2025-10-24) · Ripple written input to SEC Crypto Task Force (2026-05-22) · Ripple cross-border payments product (2026-09-01)

    What is uncertain

    • Primary sources only (Katie, 2026-10-19): official records and the actor's own documents. News, newsletters, blogs and law-firm summaries were removed on 2026-10-19; what rested on them is held in masters/_held/needs_primary_source_2026-10-19.json.
    • July deck sources carry no dates in the library; their 'date' is null unless re-verified on the web. Web sources checked on 2026-10-19 carry their publication date.
    • Technical finality, authoritative legal record and cash or redemption remedy are separate endpoints. Proposal, staff position, registration, ownership, partnership, software capability, pilot and production are different facts and clocks.
    • This is a capability-and-receipt map, not a league table, safety rating or investment view. A group can lead one surface and depend on another institution for the claim, authoritative record, cash, custody, collateral rulebook or remedy.
    • This is a functional and control comparison, not a ranking of safety, adoption, token value or investment merit. A live partner connection is not group ownership, and an approved or conditional charter is not automatically an operating service.
    • A place on this map records a bounded capability or comparison. It does not establish SEC selection, TSV qualification, a production integration, legal equivalence between models or an investment view.
    • This ledger records dated technology, deal and operating receipts. Announcements, integrations, pilots, availability, named live use and scaled use remain separate states. Company-reported activity is not independently verified volume, legal finality, token value capture or control of a third-party network.
    • The bank comparison, field guide and build-out ledger carry their own cutoffs (late September to October 3); the build-status master (October 19) is current where they differ.
    • placements.json is an index whose rows copy from their homes; its legal rows are on link E, and its countries and timeline rows belong to links H and I (not built in this wave).
    • The Major Bank Digital Transition package has no JSON registry in this workbench (README only); its comparison is read from BANK_TRANSITION_COMPARISON_2026-09-26.json.
